name: coursebook
description: Open Source Introductory Systems Programming Textbook for the University of Illinois
one_liner: A free, open textbook that teaches systems programming — how memory, processes, and the operating system actually work underneath your code — written for a university course.
buyer: Honestly, this is a free academic resource with no built-in business, not a product for a specific paying buyer.
business_use_cases: A coding bootcamp uses it as free supplementary reading for a systems-programming module instead of licensing a paid textbook.
A tutoring service builds a paid study-companion course (quizzes, office hours, exam prep) layered on top of the free open text.
A university course elsewhere adopts and forks it to save students textbook costs, citing the original.

money_ideas.idea: Sell a paid tutoring/cohort course that walks students through the free material with live support and grading.

steal_this: This weekend, package the coursebook's PDF into a self-paced video/quiz course and sell it as an affordable exam-prep companion — the content itself should stay free and open, per its license and spirit.
